question.text: Lines $x+y=1$ and $3 y=x+3$ intersect the ellipse $x^{2}+9 y^{2}=9$ at the points $P, Q$ and $R$. The area of the $\triangle P Q R$ is

solution.text: Given equation of ellipse $$ x^{2}+9 y^{2}=9 $$ $\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x^{2}}{9}+\frac{y^{2}}{1}=1$ and equation of lines $$ x+y=1 \text { and } 3 y=x+3 $$ or $\quad \frac{x}{(-3)}+\frac{y}{1}=1$ $\therefore$ Area of $\Delta P Q R=\left|\begin{array}{c|ccc}0 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 9 / 5 & -4 / 5 & 1\end{array}\right| \mid$ $=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{24}{5}+\frac{12}{5}\right]$ $=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{36}{5}=\frac{18}{5}$
